title: Section 226 — Attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power

content.overview: BNS s. 226 — Attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain the exercise of lawful power by a public servant. The general 309 offence is gone. What remains is a suicide attempt used as leverage against the State. Community service is on the menu.
In student language: BNS s. 226 is the rule on “Attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power”. The section provides that whoever attempts to commit suicide with the intent to compel or restrain any public servant from discharging his official duty shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, or with community service. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 226 exists so that “Attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Summons, proclamations, false information — and the recast suicide-attempt-to-coerce offence.

The provision in detail
226. Whoever attempts to commit suicide with the intent to compel or restrain any public servant from discharging his official duty shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, or with community service

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 226 embodies a revolutionary criminal law reform. Under colonial IPC Section 309, attempting suicide was a general criminal offence. BNS Section 226 decisively repeals that punitive approach toward mental distress. Under BNS, attempting suicide generally is completely decriminalized. Section 226 penalizes suicide attempts ONLY in one specific, coercive context: whoever attempts to commit suicide with the intent to compel or restrain any public servant from exercising their lawful power, or to force the discharge of any public duty. Punishment includes imprisonment up to one year, fine, both, or community service.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power under Section 226 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 226.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 226 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 226 BNS vs Old IPC Section 309: IPC 309 punished all suicide attempts; Section 226 punishes suicide attempts ONLY when used as coercive leverage against public servants.
Section 226 vs Section 108 (Abetment of suicide): Section 226 applies to the person attempting suicide to coerce public servants; Section 108 punishes third parties who abet a suicide.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 226 for conduct relating to attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power.
Rule: Under BNS s. 226, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 226.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 226 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
